short_description.id: Gagak berkaki tiga adalah makhluk mitologis Asia Timur yang mewakili matahari.
short_description.en: The three-legged crow is an East Asian mythological creature representing the sun.

long_description.id: Gagak berkaki tiga adalah makhluk mitologis Asia Timur yang mewakili matahari. Dalam kisah Tiongkok, nama Yangwu dan Jinwu merujuk pada gagak matahari.
long_description.en: The three-legged crow is an East Asian mythological creature representing the sun. Chinese tales use Yangwu and Jinwu for the sun crow.

long_description.id: Shanhaijing memuat penyebutan gagak berkaki tiga. Gagak dalam cakram matahari muncul pada lambang pakaian resmi kekaisaran. Gagak matahari sering diberi warna merah meski disebut gagak emas. Gagak ini juga digambarkan bersama Ibu Suri dari Barat.
long_description.en: The Shanhaijing includes a reference to the three-legged crow. The crow in a solar disc appears among symbols on formal imperial garments. The sun crow is often colored red despite the name golden crow. This crow is also portrayed with the Queen Mother of the West.

long_description.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Lunheng bahwa kaum sarjana menyebut ada gagak berkaki tiga di dalam matahari, dan Zhang Heng menulis bahwa matahari menumpuk menjadi gagak yang bertiga jari kaki. Shanhaijing menyebut satu matahari tiba dan satu keluar, semuanya dibawa gagak, sedangkan Huainanzi menceritakan bahwa setelah Yi memanah sembilan matahari, semua gagak mati.
long_description.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Lunheng saying that scholars place a three-legged crow in the sun, and Zhang Heng writes that the sun accumulates into a crow with three toes. The Shanhaijing says one sun arrives while another goes out, all carried by crows, while the Huainanzi tells that after Yi shot nine suns the crows all died.

long_description.id: Kuodi tu yang dikutip Taiping Yulan menyebut gagak berkaki tiga mengambilkan makanan bagi Xiwangmu, dan Sima Xiangru menulis bahwa gagak itu menjadi suruhannya. Tang shu mencatat seekor gagak berkaki tiga yang dipersembahkan pada tahun pertama Tianshou; Ruizong berkata kaki depannya palsu, dan tak lama kemudian satu kaki jatuh.
long_description.en: The Kuodi tu quoted in the Taiping Yulan says the three-legged crow fetches food for Xiwangmu, and Sima Xiangru writes that it served as her messenger. The Tang shu records a three-legged crow presented in the first year of Tianshou; Ruizong said its front foot was false, and shortly afterwards one foot fell.

role.id: Gagak-gagak yang mati ketika matahari dipanah
role.en: The crows that die when the suns are shot

summary.id: Menurut Huainanzi yang dikutip Taiping Yulan, pada zaman Yao sepuluh matahari muncul bersamaan dan Yi memanah sembilan di antaranya; semua gagak mati dan sayapnya jatuh.
summary.en: According to the Huainanzi as quoted in the Taiping Yulan, ten suns appeared together in Yao's time and Yi shot nine of them; the crows all died and their wings fell.

note.id: Gagak berkaki tiga digambarkan bersama Ibu Suri dari Barat dan disebut suruhannya; Kuodi tu menyebutnya mengambilkan makanan baginya.
note.en: The three-legged crow is depicted with the Queen Mother of the West and called her messenger; the Kuodi tu says it fetches food for her.

sources.title: 太平御覽/0920 (羽族部七・烏)

claims.quote: The three-legged (or tripedal) crow is a mythological creature in various mythologies and arts of East Asia. It is believed to inhabit and represent the Sun.

statement.id: Gagak berkaki tiga adalah makhluk mitologis Asia Timur yang mewakili matahari.
statement.en: The three-legged crow is an East Asian mythological creature representing the sun.

claims.quote: The Chinese have several versions of crow and crow-Sun tales. But the most popular depiction and myth of the Sun crow is that of the Yangwu or Jinwu, the "golden crow". It has also been found figured on ancient coins from Lycia and Pamphylia.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Tiongkok, nama Yangwu dan Jinwu merujuk pada gagak matahari.
statement.en: Chinese tales use Yangwu and Jinwu for the sun crow.

claims.quote: It is also mentioned in the Shanhaijing. The earliest known depiction of a three-legged crow appears in Neolithic pottery of the Yangshao culture.

statement.id: Shanhaijing memuat penyebutan gagak berkaki tiga.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing includes a reference to the three-legged crow.

claims.quote: The sanzuwu in a disc represents the sun and is also one of the Twelve Ornaments that is used in the decoration of formal imperial garments in ancient China.

statement.id: Gagak dalam cakram matahari muncul pada lambang pakaian resmi kekaisaran.
statement.en: The crow in a solar disc appears among symbols on formal imperial garments.

claims.quote: The most popular depiction and myth of a sanzuwu is of a sun crow called the Yangwu (陽烏), more commonly referred to as the Jinwu (金烏; 'golden crow') or "golden crow". Even though it is described as a corvid, it is usually coloured red instead of black.

statement.id: Gagak matahari sering diberi warna merah meski disebut gagak emas.
statement.en: The sun crow is often colored red despite the name golden crow.

claims.quote: The sanzuwu is also depicted with the Queen Mother of the West who are believed to be her messengers.

statement.id: Gagak ini juga digambarkan bersama Ibu Suri dari Barat.
statement.en: This crow is also portrayed with the Queen Mother of the West.

claims.quote: 《論衡》曰：儒者言：日中有三足烏。日，火也。烏入火中燋爛，安得立？然烏，日氣也。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan (太平御覽) mengutip Lunheng (論衡): kaum sarjana (儒者) mengatakan di dalam matahari ada burung gagak berkaki tiga (三足烏); matahari adalah api, dan gagak yang masuk ke dalam api akan hangus, tetapi gagak adalah "qi matahari" (日氣).
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan (太平御覽) quotes the Lunheng (論衡): the scholars (儒者) say there is a three-legged crow (三足烏) in the sun; the sun is fire and a crow entering fire would be scorched, yet the crow is the "qi of the sun" (日氣).

claims.quote: 張衡《靈憲》曰：日，陽精之宗，積而成烏。烏有三趾，陽之數類竒。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Lingxian (靈憲) karya Zhang Heng (張衡): matahari adalah induk esensi "yang" (陽精之宗), yang menumpuk dan menjadi gagak; gagak punya tiga jari kaki (三趾), dan angka itu tergolong ganjil seperti bilangan "yang" (陽之數類竒).
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Lingxian (靈憲) of Zhang Heng (張衡): the sun is the ancestor of the yang essence (陽精之宗), which accumulates and becomes a crow; the crow has three toes (三趾), and the number is of the odd kind belonging to yang.

claims.quote: 《括地圗》曰：崑崙之弱水中，非乘龍不得至。有三足神烏，為西王母取食。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Kuodi tu (括地圗): di perairan Ruoshui di Kunlun, yang tak bisa dicapai tanpa menunggang naga, ada gagak gaib berkaki tiga (三足神烏) yang mengambilkan makanan bagi Xiwangmu (西王母).
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Kuodi tu (括地圗): in the Ruoshui waters of Kunlun, which cannot be reached without riding a dragon, there is a divine three-legged crow (三足神烏) that fetches food for Xiwangmu (西王母, Queen Mother of the West).

claims.quote: 司馬相如《大人賦》曰：吾乃覩西王母，皜然白首母，戴勝而穴處，有三足烏為之使。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Daren fu (大人賦) karya Sima Xiangru (司馬相如): sang penyair melihat Xiwangmu (西王母) beruban putih, bermahkota sheng (戴勝), tinggal di gua, dan seekor gagak berkaki tiga (三足烏) menjadi suruhannya (為之使).
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Daren fu (大人賦) of Sima Xiangru (司馬相如): the poet sees Xiwangmu (西王母), white-haired, wearing a sheng headdress (戴勝) and living in a cave, with a three-legged crow (三足烏) serving as her messenger (為之使).

claims.quote: 《淮南子》曰：堯時，十日並出。堯命羿仰射十日，中其九。烏皆死，墮其翼。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Huainanzi (淮南子): pada zaman Yao (堯) sepuluh matahari muncul bersamaan; Yao menyuruh Yi (羿) memanah sepuluh matahari itu dan mengenai sembilan di antaranya, lalu semua gagak (烏) mati dan sayapnya jatuh.
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Huainanzi (淮南子): in the time of Yao (堯) ten suns appeared together; Yao ordered Yi (羿) to shoot at the ten suns and he hit nine of them, whereupon the crows (烏) all died and their wings fell.

claims.quote: 《唐書》曰： 天授元年，有進三足烏者，天后以為周室嘉應。睿宗時為皇嗣，言曰：「烏前足偽也。」天后不恱。須臾，一足墮地，果如其言。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Tang shu (唐書): pada tahun pertama Tianshou (天授) seseorang mempersembahkan gagak berkaki tiga dan Tianhou (天后) menganggapnya pertanda baik bagi dinasti Zhou (周室嘉應); Ruizong (睿宗), yang kala itu putra mahkota (皇嗣), berkata kaki depan gagak itu palsu (偽), dan tak lama kemudian satu kaki jatuh ke tanah.
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Tang shu (唐書): in the first year of Tianshou (天授) someone presented a three-legged crow, and Tianhou (天后) took it as an auspicious response for the Zhou house (周室嘉應); Ruizong (睿宗), then the imperial heir (皇嗣), said the crow's front foot was false (偽), and shortly afterwards one foot fell to the ground.

claims.quote: 大荒之中，有山名曰孽搖頵羝，上有扶木，柱三百里，其葉如芥。有谷曰溫源谷。湯谷上有扶木。一日方至，一日方出，皆載于烏。

statement.id: Shanhaijing (山海經), Dahuang dong jing, menyebut di Tanggu (湯谷) ada pohon fusang (扶木); ketika satu matahari tiba, satu matahari lain keluar, dan semuanya dibawa oleh gagak (載于烏).
statement.en: The Shanhaijing (山海經), Dahuang dong jing, says that at Tanggu (湯谷) there is a fusang tree (扶木); as one sun arrives another goes out, and all are carried by crows (載于烏).

gaps.searched: Ilustrasi dalam artikel tidak dipakai tanpa pemeriksaan berkas Commons, kecocokan subjek, dan lisensinya; belum ada gambar yang terverifikasi untuk entri ini.

Sumber tambahan dari Wikisource Mandarin: Taiping Yulan juan 920 (memuat kutipan Lunheng, Zhang Heng, Kuodi tu, Sima Xiangru, Huainanzi, Tang shu) dan Shanhaijing Dahuang dong jing. Huainanzi Jingshen xun (踆烏) dibuka tetapi tidak menyebut tiga kaki, sehingga tidak dipakai.
Bagian lain (kemampuan, kelemahan, penggambaran modern) tidak diisi karena belum ada kutipan yang mendukungnya.
